newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Slow Australian stocks amble to flat finish.
newsitem.headline: Slow Australian stocks amble to flat finish.

text.p: A dull Australian share market ambled to a flat finish on Friday, the big banks bolstering a soft industrial sector while the miners saw recent gains trimmed as base metals prices took a breather offshore.
The All Ordinaries index lost just 0.8 points to 2,435.5.
Despite an initial flurry of opening activity, buying interest quickly waned and by mid-morning the benchmark had found the six point range in which it spent the rest of the day.

"The banks have had a great day and the golds had a bit of a bounce back but it has been a quiet day," said Greg Matthews, executive director of Australian equities at Mercantile Mutual Investment Management Ltd.
Recent star performer Pasminco retreated after running ahead of itself on the zinc price rally in offshore markets. Its shares closed 10 cents lower at A$2.22 (US$1.73)

Shares in Burns Philp continued to sag, losing three cents to A$2.15, after brokers downgraded profit forecasts for the troubled food group while Grand Hotel shares leapt 11 cents to A$1.90 on Thursday's late announcement of the sellout by reluctant 39 percent shareholder, ING Barings.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about four to three, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
